note: Gunnison NF (Gunnison RD) campground off US-50 on Forest Road 888, ~9,300 ft, a few miles west of the Continental Divide, among scattered conifers beside a willow-lined creek. Four-wheel and OHV/ATV scenic driving nearby. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov: confirmed 23 sites, FCFS, $14, vault toilets, non-potable hand-pump water, no hookups. Added season May 23 - Oct 1, day-use and extra-vehicle fees, fees checked 2026. Note rewritten: field facts and the unsourced road description and 'max RV ~30 ft' claim dropped.
flags: Length: no agency figure. The old note's 'max RV length ~30 ft with a few longer sites, so a 23-ft rig fits easily' had no FS or recreation.gov source (recreation.gov has one placeholder Scan & Pay site, no lengths); dropped from the note. No max_rig_ft was stored. Nothing singles the campground out for small rigs.

Road: the FS page says only 'Take U.S. Highway 50 to Forest Road #888.' The old note's '~6 mi paved plus ~2 mi dirt ... RV-passable (no 4WD)' had no agency source and was dropped. No 4WD/high-clearance wording found; GMUG's conditions page says to call the Gunnison RD (970-641-0471) for road conditions.

Phone: stored 970-641-0471 is the Gunnison Ranger District, confirmed by https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/conditions ('Please contact the Gunnison Ranger District front office for road condition updates at 970-641-0471').

Water: the FS page's current conditions say 'Water available at the hand pump.' while its amenity table says 'Potable water is not available at this site.' Kept potable_water false; a human may want to ask whether the pump water is now treated.

Closures: none. The FS page shows a 'Site Closed' badge (last updated September 29, 2026), consistent with the season ending Oct. 1. The only GMUG alert linked (Gold Mountain Fire) is on the Ouray RD and does not name FR 888.

Waterfront (stored creekside, kept but worth a re-audit): Esri topo draws a small stream running NE-SW along the southeast edge of the loops and through the south end of the campground; on imagery it is a willow-lined channel ~3-5 m wide, visible in the open meadow ~150 m SW of the pin but under willows/conifers alongside the sites. No agency page mentions a creek; the old note called it Tomichi Creek. Whether a creek this small earns creekside is a judgement for the gate.
Pin 38.52144,-106.41579 = the FS point and the single recreation.gov site point, at the entrance off FR 888 with the loops just south/southeast; fine.
